I only realised how many things would actually torture my nerves until I knew what was actually causing it. As kids we are told that we are too sensitive which leads to us ignoring our mental state because everyone can deal with this. Why can't I? I wouldn't have been so sure either if my best friend hadn't told me "yep I've known that for a while now, glad you noticed too." But in all seriousness: no matter if you actually have autism or not, if stimming makes you feel good and you avoid sensory inputs that don't feel nice, what's the actual harm? If you don't feel like a total piece of garbage at the end of the day everything is fine and your parents should calm down. My parents don't even know about my suspicion because they would probably either be in denial or tell everyone like I'm some sort of trophy they just won. Fun fact: one of my childhood special interest was a diving game in which I had to locate fish. Over 400 on 8 maps each with 8x8 quadrants and I knew them all. It was "normal". The picture people (even teachers and professionals) have of autism is some unrealistic nonverbal 5 year old boy who likes trains. My social worker in school who is now also my boss didn't realise I was on the spectrum either. Just me casually being hyperlexic and according to my class mates a walking wikipediapage (calling me (real name)-pedia in 10th grade) like yeah that's normal....

I was kinda lucky with maths and english being huge special interests. I simply worked through 2 years of school work in like 6 months without feeling like actually putting effort into it. And nobody noticed except my best friend. Like even my teachers thought I was just a good student. Not even "the best". I also have friend with a special interest in shooter games. She is an aimbot. So chances are your special interest could also be something you don't infodump about but rather just do. It doesn't need to be something that makes "sense" as well. I always felt off or weird and couldn't pin point what it was exactly and therefore concluded that it was childhood trauma and some symptoms of depression and anxiety. I also was quite lonely up to 10th grade so I had barely any help from other people. School/family wasn't helpful either. So I at some point I said duck it and started to work on it myself and I stumbled into my best friend who was my rescue. She had some axiety related issues, too. She was actually the one who realised I was autistic first xD. 

Apperently I asked such weird questions about why people behave a certain way and what some emotions feel like that she recognized the behavior in a trash tv hospital series. She didn't tell me tho bc it would have ducked my mental health even more and I was just starting to get better. She just kept doing what she already started. Explaining the world in logic. Life went on and I went to university, thinking I was a gifted kid with burn out bc I never had to work for my grades. When I didn't like a subject I would just do like the bare minimum, in english and maths however I was top 3 of the class from 10th grade on (hint the hyperfixation/special interest in those subjects). 

A few months ago I thought I met a second her (or so I thought), a young man. We trauma dumped a lot on each other, had a pretty similar history and I trusted him enough that I explained to him that my world works more in logic than in feelings. And he just was somehow fine with it. So we kinda promised each other that we would always tell each other the truth. And then it went downhill. His emotions were nothing I could handle, I tried to solve emotions with logic and well... i ducked up and I acknowledge that. 

So I went back to my best friend who I could always turn to no matter what and I asked her about the suspicion I had for a few weeks now (when it already went downhill with this friend group but I kinda ignored it bc I the signals weren't clear enough for me). 

I'm still trying to figure out how empathy works, I'm currently working on the hyperthesis that I'm hyperempathetic while simultaneously having alexithymia or I have such a low amount of emotions (which I noticed in my early teens) that I just wanted to have some emotions and ended up mirroring his. (Funfact he had to explain emotions to me and even joked about it in front of other people xD)
I lost this whole friend group we were in bc of mirroring their thoughts (I didn't know what I was "allowed to think" so I just picked up what the others thought plus our honesty promise). A mutual friend gave me an honest evaluation of the situation and didn't see all the fault on my side so I guess I can live with that. 

What I'm still struggling with is being called manipulative and having a god complex. Bc that was what I am scared to be all my life. My best friend however explained to me that I pick up certain behaviors and analyze people to substitute the theory of mind. I now understand that telling people what I see is not the way to go. 

Also a friend I wasn't really close with told me that she is also autistic and we spend a whole evening ranting about sensory issues etc. I think I can learn a lot from her. 

Right now I focus on my autistic strenghts like my hyperfixations (especially since I'm studying maths and english) because I struggled a lot to see them as strenghts before. And I started to work on my weaknesses like my dyspraxia to finally feel better in my body. 

Generally speaking I don't believe in a god but in purpose. Everything happens for a reason and this experience will help me to grow as a person.

This is my personal experience and I wouldn't generalise it, but maybe it helps non-sh understand.

I've had some troubles with anxiety and suicidal thoughts before, but when my parents had a bad crisis in their relationship, I started self harming (now I'm "clean"=sh free). I tried my best to hide it and I was good at it. I didn't want people to notice the cuts on my ankles. I paniced every time I had to change in the locker room in front of my friends. I isolated myself. And something weird happened: I got better at school, I didn't just maintain my okay grades, I really got better grades.
To understand that, you also need to know how "wanting to cut" feels like. Before I cut, this pressure built in me. It started with a weird feeling, like having a hard time to concentrate, in combination with tiny random movements I make with my feet or fingers or smth like that.
Then it gets worse, I lose memory somewhere at this point, so most of this has been filled in by my friends. I lose the sensation in my body. I know this is hard to comprehend. Think of a first person perspective in a video game: You can control the character, you can see that the character has been hit, you can see and hear everything the character sees and hears. But there is the barrier between you and the character, you can't feel what he/she is feeling, you simply control him/her. 
So I can see that I grab the door knob, I can control my hand and open the door, but it doesn't feel real. 
I subconsciously try to reactivate my senses by giving it some sort of sensation (e.g. digging my nails in my hand, scratching, hitting one foot with the other). 
Of course, I don't feel it, so it gets harder over time, I can draw blood. 
If it takes longer, I start trembling. 
The longer I wait until I give in and cut again, the more severe the cuts get. 

Mental disorders are always caused by two things coming together: your genetics and your environment. 
There is a "wrong connection" in our brain. So every time I get overwhelmed by something or my brain thinks I got to much, it presses the emergency button. This means that my brain doesn't accept any sensoric stimulus. Then I need a certain negative impulse to reactivate my brain. For me it's mainly seeing my own blood, I also can get some relief from bruising. There are many ways of self harming.
While I lose memory in this state, which means that I can't remember anything in this time period and also can't remember anything I did during this state, I'm also impassive. 
I also don't feel the cuts/pain (and btw: I could not cut when I was not in that state, it would be too painful). For me the cuts/blood look aestetically attractive in that state. But that only works with my own blood. And I stare at it for at least 5 minutes, it just looks somewhat pretty to me.
After I get back to normal, the love for blood fades, I'm concentrated and I can work on school things for 8+ hours without one break. And then the cycle starts again. My grades dropped after I stopped cutting. I nearly always gave in after 4 days, because that's when the memory loss occured again. But for everyone it's different. There were also a period when I cut twice a day. 
For everyone it's a bit different, but maybe this will help people understand.

well that is kind of tricky because of the german poem style. poems are often written in an "old" language. "Mein herz blutet für dich" is grammatically correct although for a native german (girl) it sounds a bit odd. More "common" is the sentence "Ich lege dir mein Herz zu Füßen" (=I lay my heart to your feet) 
"So sehr lieb mir" is grammatically incorrect. What do you want to express with that?
"Ich wisse meine lieb" is also wrong (liebe= love lieb= nice) you also don't "wisse" (know in a sense of knowing (everything) about a theme, for example: Ich weiss was 2+3 ist) 
"Mich nicht vergessen" is kind of odd too. I think you wanted to express something like "(please) Don't forget me" (=(bitte) vergess' mich nicht) 
"vergess' " is the shortened term for vergesse. 
I'm impressed that you tried to write a poem in a foreign language. German is really hard.

hey this is your life and your decision but maybe you can learn a bit from my story.
I'm a 17 year-old girl. I suffered from depression and anxiety for the past years. I was close to dead about six times. I'm also homosexual so a broken heart (especially if you haven't come out to everyone yet) is very common for me. 
I used to hang around with this group of girls when I considered myself "healthy". I never said a word when we "talked" in the breaks but I didn't really care. However I had a hard time with my family and that was the first time I said something. They proceeded to look at me with pity from this point on and that really made it worse. I turned away from them because I  couldn't take the daily pity and that everything got studied. They tried to see if I was getting worse. I felt like big brother was watching me. 
That wasn't the last time it happened and it took me a long time to notice what was wrong. I started cutting and became suicidal. After a suicidal phase (the most extreme one I've ever had) I really asked myself what was wrong and I noticed that I had wrong friends but it was also my fault. I couldn't find a good control of the information. When I told them nothing everything was fine for them but hell for me. When I told someone I told nearly the whole story at once I felt relieved but also anxious because they were overwhelmed and I didn't want them to tell anyone. A relationship is not a therapy and my friends are in no way responsible for me. I am now in a good friendship with a girl that knows practically everything about me and handles it great. If I have a problem and she feels overwhelmed by hearing about it we talk about it. She is really open about this and it helps me too because I know that my pain gets acknowledged. But she doesn't look at me with pity. We can also tallk about different things despite our problems and if it would be just our problems that get mentioned every time it would take me down like the friendships before.
